cards.translation: linha de assunto; assunto do e-mail
cards.definition: The short title that indicates what an email is about.
cards.example:
- Write a clear subject line before sending the email.
Escreva um assunto claro antes de enviar o e-mail.
- The subject line did not explain the purpose of the message.
A linha de assunto não explicava o objetivo da mensagem.
- I changed the subject line to make the email easier to find.
Eu alterei o assunto para facilitar a localização do e-mail.
cards.note: “Subject line” é o campo de assunto do e-mail. Use frases curtas e específicas, como “Updated Sales Report” ou “Meeting Rescheduled”.

cards.definition: The folder where new email messages are received.
cards.example:
- I check my inbox first thing in the morning.
Eu verifico minha caixa de entrada logo pela manhã.
- Her inbox was full after the vacation.
A caixa de entrada dela estava cheia depois das férias.
- The confirmation email should be in your inbox.
O e-mail de confirmação deve estar na sua caixa de entrada.
cards.note: “Inbox” é a pasta onde chegam novas mensagens. “Outbox” é a caixa de saída, e “sent folder” é a pasta de mensagens enviadas.

cards.definition: To answer a message, email, or question.
cards.example:
- Please reply to the customer before noon.
Por favor, responda ao cliente antes do meio-dia.
- She replied to my email yesterday.
Ela respondeu ao meu e-mail ontem.
- I am still waiting for his reply.
Eu ainda estou esperando a resposta dele.
cards.note: “Reply” pode ser verbo ou substantivo. Como verbo, use “reply to”: “reply to an email”. O passado e o particípio são “replied”.

cards.translation: colocar em cópia; copiar alguém no e-mail
cards.definition: To send a copy of an email to an additional recipient.
cards.example:
- Please cc the project manager on the email.
Por favor, coloque o gerente do projeto em cópia no e-mail.
- She cc'd me on the message to the client.
Ela me colocou em cópia na mensagem para o cliente.
- I will cc the finance team so they can follow the discussion.
Vou colocar a equipe financeira em cópia para que acompanhe a discussão.
cards.note: “CC” significa “carbon copy”. Use “cc someone on an email”. Para esconder os destinatários copiados, use “BCC”, que significa “blind carbon copy”.

cards.definition: An unfinished version of a document, message, or email.
cards.example:
- I saved the email as a draft.
Eu salvei o e-mail como rascunho.
- She sent me the first draft of the report.
Ela me enviou o primeiro rascunho do relatório.
- Please review the draft before I send it to the client.
Por favor, revise o rascunho antes que eu o envie ao cliente.
cards.note: “Draft” é uma versão ainda não finalizada. É comum dizer “first draft”, “final draft”, “save as a draft” e “draft an email”.

cards.definition: A small mistake made while typing a word or text.
cards.example:
- I noticed a typo in the subject line.
Eu percebi um erro de digitação no assunto.
- The email had two typos, so I corrected them.
O e-mail tinha dois erros de digitação, então eu os corrigi.
- A simple typo changed the meaning of the sentence.
Um simples erro de digitação mudou o sentido da frase.
cards.note: “Typo” é uma forma informal e muito comum de “typographical error”. Refere-se a erro de digitação, não necessariamente a erro gramatical.

cards.translation: segue anexo; favor encontrar em anexo
cards.definition: A formal email phrase used to indicate that a file is included with the message.
cards.example:
- Please find attached the updated contract.
Segue anexo o contrato atualizado.
- Please find attached my résumé for your review.
Segue anexo meu currículo para sua análise.
- Please find the requested spreadsheet attached.
Segue anexa a planilha solicitada.
cards.note: “Please find attached” é correto, mas bastante formal. Em e-mails mais naturais, use “I’ve attached the report” ou “The report is attached”.

cards.term: I look forward to hearing from you
cards.ipa: /aɪ lʊk ˈfɔːrwərd tə ˈhɪrɪŋ frəm juː/
cards.translation: aguardo seu retorno; fico no aguardo de sua resposta
cards.definition: A polite closing phrase used to say that you expect or hope to receive a response.
cards.example:
- I look forward to hearing from you soon.
Aguardo seu retorno em breve.
- Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.
Obrigado pelo seu tempo. Fico no aguardo de sua resposta.
- We look forward to hearing from you after the meeting.
Aguardamos seu retorno depois da reunião.
cards.note: Depois de “look forward to”, use substantivo ou verbo com “-ing”: “look forward to hearing”, não “look forward to hear”. É uma frase educada e comum no fechamento de e-mails.

cards.definition: Showing good judgment and making practical decisions.
cards.example:
- That sounds like a sensible solution.
Isso parece uma solução sensata.
- She made a sensible decision based on the available data.
Ela tomou uma decisão razoável com base nos dados disponíveis.
- It would be sensible to back up the files first.
Seria sensato fazer backup dos arquivos primeiro.
cards.note: “Sensible” significa sensato ou razoável. Não significa “sensível”. Para “sensível”, use “sensitive”.

cards.definition: To become aware of or understand something clearly.
cards.example:
- I realized that I had attached the wrong file.
Eu percebi que havia anexado o arquivo errado.
- She did not realize the meeting had been canceled.
Ela não percebeu que a reunião havia sido cancelada.
- We realized the mistake before sending the email.
Nós percebemos o erro antes de enviar o e-mail.
cards.note: “Realize” geralmente significa perceber ou dar-se conta, não realizar no sentido de executar. Para “realizar uma tarefa”, use “carry out”, “perform” ou “complete”. O passado é “realized”.

questions.prompt: Which part of an email briefly tells the reader what the message is about?
questions.explanation: The “subject line” is the short title that describes the purpose of an email.

questions.prompt: Please _____ to the customer before the end of the day.
questions.explanation: “Reply” means to answer a message or email.

questions.prompt: Por favor, coloque o gerente em cópia no e-mail.
questions.answer: Please cc the manager on the email.|Please CC the manager on the email.
questions.explanation: Use “cc someone on an email” when sending that person a copy.

questions.prompt: Which word describes a practical decision based on good judgment?
questions.explanation: “Sensible” means practical and based on good judgment.

questions.prompt: I have not finished the email yet, so I saved it as a _____.
questions.explanation: A “draft” is an unfinished version of a document or message.

questions.answer: Please find attached the updated report.|Please find the updated report attached.
questions.explanation: “Please find attached” is a formal way to indicate that a file is included.

questions.prompt: You accidentally type “manger” instead of “manager.” What is this?
questions.explanation: A “typo” is a small mistake made while typing.

questions.prompt: The confirmation email should be waiting in your _____.
questions.explanation: The “inbox” is the folder where new email messages are received.

questions.target: I look forward to hearing from you
questions.answer: I look forward to hearing from you soon.|I look forward to hearing from you.
questions.explanation: This is a polite phrase used to close an email and express that you expect a response.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means that someone suddenly became aware of a mistake?
options: She realized the file was missing.
questions.answer: She realized the file was missing.
questions.explanation: “Realize” means to become aware of or understand something clearly.
